scope: Primary sources for joints and sustained load, read as stated; the gusts, air and storms are committed project products named in structure.py INPUT_FILES.

sources.citation: Wood, L. W. (1951). Relation of strength of wood to duration of load. USDA Forest Products Laboratory Report No. 1916 (reaffirmed reprint).
sources.access: Full text of the reaffirmed reprint read by a verification agent on 2026-10-09.
sources.use: Madison curve y = 108.4/x^0.04635 + 18.3, x seconds under load, y percent of the standard ~5-minute static bending strength; fitted through (0.015 s, 150%), (7.5 min, 100%) and (3,750 h, 69%); 126 long-time tests on clear Douglas fir begun in 1943. 10 years gives 62%.
sources.limit: Wood in bending at 6% and 12% moisture content. Used as the measured biological analogue for a cellulose fibre composite; a floater fibre needs its own curve. The often-quoted SL = 108.4 - 9.31 log10(T) form is not in the report and is not used.

sources.citation: Wang, X. T. and Ker, R. F. (1995). Creep rupture of wallaby tail tendons. Journal of Experimental Biology 198(3), 831-845.
sources.use: Creep rupture occurs at 10 MPa and above; time to rupture falls exponentially with stress between 20 and 80 MPa, with the 10 MPa lifetime well above that line; dynamic yield about 144 MPa; isometric contraction stress about 13.5 MPa.
sources.limit: Macropus rufogriseus tail tendon in vitro; fitted constants and temperature dependence not read. The 10 MPa level anchors the collagen tendon case only.

sources.citation: Wang, X. T., Ker, R. F. and Alexander, R. McN. (1995). Fatigue rupture of wallaby tail tendons. Journal of Experimental Biology 198(3), 847-852.
sources.use: Cyclic fatigue failure is distinct from creep rupture (tests at 1-50 Hz).

sources.citation: Ker, R. F., Wang, X. T. and Pike, A. V. L. (2000). Fatigue quality of mammalian tendons. Journal of Experimental Biology 203(8), 1317-1327.
sources.use: Wallaby hind-limb tendons loaded to their muscles' maximum isometric force ruptured after about 4.2 hours on average.
sources.limit: Static loading at physiological maximum; per-tendon ultimate strengths not read.

design_guesses.note: Gust factor and decades factor follow the summit tower and sky-ship studies.
